```{python}
#| code-fold: show
faithful = pd.read_csv("data/faithful.csv")
eruptions = torch.tensor(faithful.to_numpy(), dtype=torch.float32)
center, scale = eruptions.mean(dim=0), eruptions.std(dim=0)
standardized = (eruptions - center) / scale
long_share = (eruptions[:, 0] > 3).float().mean().item()


def long_wait_sd(points):
    # Standard deviation of the wait, over the eruptions longer than 3 minutes.
    return points[points[:, 0] > 3, 1].std().item()


real_long_sd = long_wait_sd(eruptions)
print(faithful.head())
print(len(faithful), long_share, real_long_sd)
```

::: {#fig-faithful}

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "A scatter plot of 272 eruptions of Old Faithful, eruption length in minutes across and waiting time in minutes up. The points form two clusters: short eruptions near 2 minutes with waits near 55 minutes, and long eruptions near 4.5 minutes with waits near 80 minutes."
def plot_eruptions(ax, points, title):
    ax.scatter(points[:, 0], points[:, 1], s=6);
    ax.set_xlabel("eruption (minutes)");
    ax.set_ylabel("wait (minutes)");
    ax.set_title(title);


fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3.5))
plot_eruptions(ax, eruptions, "Old Faithful");
fig.tight_layout();
plt.show()
```

The length of each of the `r nrow(py$faithful)` eruptions and the wait until the next one.

:::

The rest of the lecture uses smaller data:
a local copy, [`data/faithful.csv`](data/faithful.csv),
of the `r nrow(py$faithful)` eruptions of the Old Faithful geyser in R's `faithful` data set [@r_faithful],
from @azzalini1990look.
`tools/get-faithful.R` writes the copy from R, unchanged.
Each row gives an eruption's length and the wait until the next one, in minutes.
The eruptions fall in two clusters,
and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$long_share)` of them last longer than 3 minutes.
`standardized` rescales each column to mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
